title: AI-built Baihetan reservoir catalog reveals fault-controlled and depth-dependent seismicity
summary: LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events. The authors infer that post-impoundment seismicity is concentrated along regional structures and fractures, differs across the Jinsha River, and includes migration away from the inundation zone and with depth. They report depth-dependent b-value and water-depth/event-rate patterns consistent with different shallow and deep controls.
ai_technology: LOC-FLOW automated earthquake-detection and location workflow using PhaseNet deep-learning phase picking
organization: China Earthquake Administration; Institute of Geophysics; Institute of Earthquake Forecasting

evidence.tested: LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events.
evidence.unknown: The catalog covers one reservoir and January 2021–July 2022. The reported location errors are relative errors, not absolute location accuracy. Spatial distribution and migration are observations from the catalog; proposed tectonic, lithologic, fluid-diffusion, poroelastic, water-load, and pore-pressure explanations are author interpretations and are not uniquely established by this study. The paper discusses the need to assess whether the larger automated catalog contains only genuine events. Summary claims are limited to the published abstract and article metadata checked here.
evidence.ai_role: The AI phase picker enabled automatic processing of continuous records from 55 stations into the high-resolution event catalog used for relocations and the spatiotemporal, depth, and b-value analyses. The authors report 53,838 detections, roughly four times the manual catalog, while recalling about 99% of the manual events.
